summary: Sets out a transient prefix that working groups can use for the BEEP profiles they develop. Once a profile is published as an RFC, IANA assigns a permanent identifier. It is a best current practice.

eli5.summary: While a recipe is still being tested, you pen a temporary name on it. This document says what temporary name to use for draft protocol profiles until a permanent one is given.

subtitle: How IETF working groups name BEEP profiles while they are still drafts, before IANA hands out a permanent identifier.

tldr.problem: A BEEP profile is identified by a URI, but a profile still being developed in an IETF working group has no permanent, IANA-assigned URI yet.
tldr.mechanism: The working group chair assigns a transient URI of the form http://iana.org/beep/transient/XXX/YYY, where XXX is the working group's mnemonic and YYY is a unique string, and registers it with IANA.
tldr.outcome: If the profile is later published as an RFC, IANA assigns a permanent identifier. The transient URI only covers the development period.

facts.label: XXX
facts.value: Working group mnemonic, assigned by the IETF secretariat

facts.label: YYY
facts.value: Unique string chosen by the working group chair

today: RFC 3349 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 59) and, according to the metadata for this page, has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why Profiles Need Identifiers
sections.content:
Each BEEP profile (defined in RFC 3080) is identified by a URI. BEEP uses that URI in two places: statically, when a profile is formally defined, and dynamically, during channel management.

If a profile is on the standards track, IANA is responsible for assigning its URI. Otherwise, whoever specifies the profile is free to assign a URI under their own administration.

A working group that is still developing a profile has a gap: the permanent IANA URI does not exist yet. The RFC says a transient identifier is desirable during development, and that it should be associated with the working group.
sections.eli5: Every game needs a name so players can ask for it. A game that is still being invented needs a temporary name until the real one is chosen.

sections.title: Who the Practice Applies To
sections.content:
The practice applies only to IETF working groups. The RFC notes that it does not apply to activities outside of working groups: anyone able to assign a URL can define a URI to identify the BEEP profiles they develop.

So this is a narrow administrative convention, not a general rule for naming every BEEP profile.
sections.eli5: This rule is only for the club's own projects. Anyone outside the club can name their own projects however they like.

sections.title: How a Transient Identifier Is Assigned
sections.content:
When a working group is formed, the IETF secretariat assigns it a brief mnemonic prefix, for example provreg or sacred.

When the working group starts a document that specifies a BEEP profile, the working group chair assigns an identifier of the form http://iana.org/beep/transient/XXX/YYY. XXX is the working group's mnemonic and YYY is a unique string. The result must conform to the URI syntax, but the YYY part is otherwise arbitrary and may contain a sub-hierarchy such as epp/1.0.

The chair then completes a BEEP profile registration template and submits it to IANA.
sections.eli5: The club gives each team a short nickname. The team captain writes a temporary label that starts with that nickname and sends it to the office that keeps the list.

sections.title: Examples and Capitalization
sections.content:
The RFC gives two examples of identifiers the chairs of the provreg and sacred working groups might assign: http://iana.org/beep/transient/provreg/epp/1.0 and http://iana.org/beep/transient/sacred/pdm.

On capitalization, the RFC notes that the IETF has no established practice for URLs used as namespace names, while the W3C has a lowercase-only policy. Working group chairs are encouraged to consider this.
sections.eli5: The examples show what a finished temporary label looks like. The advice is to write the label in small letters so nobody mixes up big and small ones.

sections.title: IANA Registry and Authorization
sections.content:
IANA maintains a registry of the transient identifiers used for BEEP profiles under development in the IETF. It uses the profile registration template from Section 5.1 of RFC 3080.

One difference from the normal procedure: the working group chair, rather than the IESG, authorizes the registration.

Security considerations: the RFC describes an administrative convention that raises no additional security considerations. Each BEEP-based protocol has its own, described in its own specification.
sections.eli5: The office keeps a list of all temporary labels. The team captain, not the big boss, is the one who says yes to adding a label.
